target: Vocês gostam de comida picante?
english: Do you like spicy food?
tip: 'Picante' is spicy-hot in flavor; 'quente' is hot in temperature. Comida picante burns the tongue.

target: Ele prefere café sem açúcar.
english: He prefers coffee without sugar.
tip: 'Preferir' doesn't need a preposition – just 'prefiro café' or 'prefiro ir a pé.' Unlike 'gostar de' and 'precisar de.'

target: O tempo está horrível hoje.
english: The weather is terrible today.
tip: 'Tempo' means both weather and time; 'está horrível hoje' shows it is the weather here.

target: O problema do trânsito é sério.
english: The traffic problem is serious.
tip: 'Do' is the contraction of 'de + o' (of the, masculine). These contractions are mandatory – you can never say 'de o.'

target: As ruas do centro estão cheias.
english: The downtown streets are crowded.
tip: 'Estão cheias' uses estar because crowded is the streets' condition right now, not a permanent trait; ser would sound inherent.

target: A voz dela é muito bonita.
english: Her voice is very beautiful.
tip: 'Dele/dela' = his/her. More specific than 'seu/sua' which can mean his/her/your.

target: Eu paguei a conta do restaurante.
english: I paid the restaurant bill.
tip: -gar verbs add a u in the 'eu' past to keep the hard g sound: pagar becomes paguei.

target: A foto do perfil dela é bonita.
english: Her profile picture is pretty.
tip: 'Foto' is feminine (a foto) because it's short for 'fotografia.' Similarly, 'moto' is feminine (a moto) from 'motocicleta.'

target: Tem um gato no telhado.
english: There's a cat on the roof.
tip: In Brazilian Portuguese, 'tem' is commonly used to mean 'there is/there are,' even though formal grammar prefers 'há.'

target: Os sapatos estão debaixo da cama.
english: The shoes are under the bed.
tip: For where things are located, use 'estar': os sapatos estão debaixo da cama, not 'são.'

target: Ela não gosta de acordar cedo.
english: She doesn't like waking up early.
tip: 'Gostar de' + infinitive for activities: 'não gosta de acordar.' The 'de' is always required before the verb.

target: Ela prefere morar perto do trabalho.
english: She prefers to live near work.
tip: 'Perto de' means near, and the de contracts with the article: perto + o = perto do trabalho.

target: O café está quente e forte.
english: The coffee is hot and strong.
tip: Adjectives ending in -e don't change for gender: quente is the same for masculine and feminine. Only number changes: quentes.

target: Eu falei com o gerente ontem.
english: I spoke with the manager yesterday.
tip: 'Falar com' = to speak with or to someone: falei com o gerente. Portuguese uses com where English says 'to.'

target: Eu emprestei dinheiro para um amigo.
english: I lent money to a friend.
tip: 'Emprestar' in Brazilian Portuguese means both 'to lend' and 'to borrow.' Context clarifies: 'emprestei para ele' = I lent to him. 'Emprestei DELE' = I borrowed from him.

target: As férias dos funcionários são em janeiro.
english: The employees' vacations are in January.
tip: 'Férias' is always plural in Portuguese – there's no singular form. 'As férias' = vacation(s).

target: Eu preciso de mais tempo para terminar.
english: I need more time to finish.
tip: 'Precisar de' = to need (something). Like 'gostar de,' the preposition 'de' is mandatory: 'preciso de mais tempo.'

target: A cor da parede combina com os móveis.
english: The wall color matches the furniture.
tip: 'Cor' is feminine: a cor. Some nouns don't follow the -o/-a pattern and must be memorized.

target: Nós jantamos num restaurante italiano.
english: We had dinner at an Italian restaurant.
tip: For -ar verbs the nós form is identical in present and past, so 'jantamos' can mean we dine or we dined, and context decides.

target: Ela vai à academia todo dia.
english: She goes to the gym every day.
tip: 'À' is the contraction of 'a + a' (to the, feminine). This is the famous 'crase' – it gets its own accent mark in Portuguese.

target: O problema é a falta de tempo.
english: The problem is the lack of time.
tip: 'Problema' is masculine (o problema) despite ending in -a. This is one of the most common gender mistakes learners make.

target: Eu trouxe o contrato para o escritório.
english: I brought the contract to the office.
tip: 'Trazer' (to bring) is irregular in the past: eu trouxe, not the expected 'trazi.'

target: Ele gosta de acordar cedo para correr.
english: He likes waking up early to run.
tip: Gostar always needs 'de' where English 'like' takes no preposition: it is 'gosta de acordar', and dropping the de breaks it.

target: Os pratos da comida mineira são fartos.
english: The dishes of Minas Gerais cuisine are generous.
tip: 'São fartos' uses ser because generous portions are the inherent character of mineira cooking, not a passing state.

target: Nós procuramos o restaurante por uma hora.
english: We looked for the restaurant for an hour.
tip: 'Procurar' means to look for and takes a direct object: procuramos o restaurante, with no preposition before it.

target: Meu irmão mais novo é o mais alto da família.
english: My younger brother is the tallest in the family.
tip: The superlative frame is 'o mais alto da família', where Portuguese says of the family where English says in the family.

target: A gente gosta de fazer trilha.
english: We like hiking.
tip: 'Fazer trilha' means to hike. Brazilians use 'fazer' in many leisure expressions: fazer mergulho (dive), fazer escalada (climb), fazer rapel (rappel).

target: Vocês gostam de churrasco?
english: Do you like barbecue?
tip: Unlike Spanish gustar, Portuguese gostar keeps normal order: subject plus 'gostam de churrasco', with no subject flip.

target: A comida está deliciosa.
english: The food is delicious.
tip: Adjectives agree in gender: 'deliciosa' (fem.) matches 'comida' (fem.). Masculine would be 'delicioso.'

target: Desculpa, eu não entendi.
english: Sorry, I didn't understand.
tip: Desculpa is the casual sorry; Desculpe is more formal. Brazilians say Desculpa with friends and family.
